verdict.rationale: Checkout.com's issuing docs say ops can manage cardholders' spending limits and velocity and set granular transaction-amount limits. They also say Checkout.com can make authorization decisions itself through spend controls, so the platform enforces them rather than customer code. However, the evidence never spells out the time windows, the per-card versus per-cardholder scoping, or how count-based velocity rules work. Missing for 10: explicit daily/monthly/all-time limit windows, documented per-card vs per-cardholder limit scoping, transaction-count velocity rule details, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can set spend limits per card and per cardholder — amount caps over daily, monthly, or all-time windows, and transaction-count velocity rules — enforced by the platform, not my code
